title: Organic re-initiate does not clear a stale rt_first_touch cookie left by an abandoned attempt, so the callback attributes the new signup to the old attempt's paid params
evidence:
case first_touch_cookie.from_initiate_query(wisp.get_query(req)) {
        [] -> response
        pairs ->
          response
          |> wisp.set_cookie(
            req,
            cookie_names.first_touch(),
            first_touch_cookie.cookie_value(pairs),
            wisp.Signed,
            first_touch_cookie.max_age,
          )
      }

(handler comment, lines 1000-1001: "No params (organic landing)
// → no cookie — the callback then falls back to `provider=google`.")

first_touch_cookie.gleam:17: "// as the PKCE verifier), and cleared on every terminal OAuth response."
detail: If attempt 1 sets the cookie (paid landing) and the user abandons at Google (no callback → no terminal clear), a second organic initiate within 300s hits the `[] -> response` branch, which neither overwrites nor clears the cookie; the callback then permanently locks the stale paid params via $set_once, contradicting the documented "no cookie → provider=google" guarantee.
recommended_fix: In the `[] -> response` branch, also apply `first_touch_cookie.clear_cookie(response, req)` so every initiate is set-or-clear and stale attribution can never survive into a later flow.
